    About this tradition

    What is the Chinese zodiac?

    The twelve animals (生肖) name the twelve Earthly Branches, an ancient Chinese way of counting years, months and hours. Combined with the ten Heavenly Stems, they make a cycle of sixty years that is still printed on Chinese calendars.

    Popular tradition gives each animal a character. These associations are folk tradition, with no single classical source, and Fate Tutor labels them that way.

    Two calendars give two start dates for the year: Lunar New Year (the popular way) and Start of Spring, 立春 (the way BaZi counts). For most birthdays they agree; for births between late January and mid February they can differ, and this page shows both.

    These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
